newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-GOUGH AND CROFT COMBINE TO THWART AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GOUGH AND CROFT COMBINE TO THWART AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Darren Gough and Robert Croft, two of the successes of England's winter tour, conbined forces again on Thursday to hold Australia to 170 for eight in the first one-day international at Headingley.
Gough, at his vibrant best before his home Yorkshire crowd on a dark, cold day, took a wicket in two of his three spells to finish with two for 33 from 10 controlled overs.

He prolonged Australian captain Mark Taylor's miserable international trot in his second over with the new ball then returned to dismiss Greg Blewett at a time when the sun briefly shone and the elegant South Australian was starting to look dangerous.

Croft did not take a wicket, although he had Ian Healy badly dropped at square leg by Graham Thorpe. But his 10 overs of thoughtful off-spin cost only 16 runs as England put a stranglehold on the touring team.
Taylor's lack of decisive foot movement betrayed him in Gough's second over when he waved at a delivery outside the off stump and nicked the ball to wicketkeeper Alec Stewart after scoring seven.
The Waugh twins found stroke-making difficult once DeFreitas found a length, with Mark taking 20 balls to get off the mark and Steve needing 16.
Both perished to indifferent shots within the space of six balls after adding 31 for the second wicket.

Mark Waugh played across a full straight delivery from newcomer Dean Headley and was bowled for 11 then Steve was lbw to Ealham's gentle medium-pace for 19, shuffling indeterminately across his stumps.
Left-hander Michael Bevan, who represented Yorkshire with distinction last season, combined with Blewett to add 50 in 14.2 overs.
But then Bevan was run out for 30 when Thorpe threw down the stumps at the bowler's end.
Gough compounded Australia's woes with his next ball when Blewett dragged a full delivery on to the middle stump. Blewett, who had looked the most comfortable of the Australian batmen, made 28.

Healy nudged and sliced to some effect before he was caught by a diving Mike Atherton off Adam Hollioake for 17 and Ealham held a a stinging return catch to dismiss Michael Slater, batting down the order at number six, also for 17.
The Australian tailenders could not break the England stranglehold.
